article_title: Microsoft Scales Hollow-Core Fiber for AI Data Centers With Corning and Heraeus After Setting a 0.091 dB/km Fiber-Loss Record

content_preview.title: Microsoft Scales Hollow-Core Fiber for AI Data Centers With Corning and Heraeus After Setting a 0.091 dB/km Fiber-Loss Record
content_preview.summary: Microsoft is moving hollow-core fiber from pilot to production for Azure, partnering with Corning and Heraeus after a research team recorded the lowest optical-fiber loss ever measured, 0.091 dB/km.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Microsoft is moving hollow-core fiber (HCF) from pilot deployments toward volume production for its Azure network. In late September 2025 the company named Corning and Heraeus as manufacturing partners to build what it calls a resilient, global supply chain for the technology, [as reported by Data Center Dynamics](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/microsoft-ramps-up-hollow-core-fiber-production-with-corning-heraeus-partnerships/). The push follows a research result, publish...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured Analysis piece (1,042 words, within the 800-2000 band). Clear progression from the production news, to a plain-language explainer of hollow-core fiber, to the loss record, deployment history, the manufacturing deals, a parallel microLED project, an honest 'What We Don't Know' section, and a grounded Analysis close. Technical depth is appropriate for a general-technical audience.

editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific number (0.091 dB/km, 0.14 dB/km, 18 THz, seven-fold dispersion, 47% / 33%, 3x bandwidth, 33 km vs 15-20 km, 1,200 km pilot, 15,000 km Azure target, 40 km Comcast, 45 km euNetworks, 32/48 hybrid strands, 50% microLED energy, late 2027, 2022 acquisition) traces to the correct cited source. All five direct quotes appear verbatim in their snapshots and are attributed to the correct speaker and outlet (Gaudette->DCD, Poletti live-traffic->Network World, Poletti average-loss->The Register, Poletti distortions->IEEE Spectrum). The headline record figure and the summary are both directly supported by Network World and The Register. No hallucinations detected.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and measured. The piece consistently attributes claims to Microsoft ('Microsoft says,' 'the company claims,' 'by Microsoft's account') rather than asserting vendor figures as fact, includes a dedicated 'What We Don't Know' caveat section, and the closing Analysis is interpretive but grounded in the cited standardization and manufacturing-economics points from The Register and DCD rather than editorializing.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. No prior Machine Herald coverage of hollow-core fiber or Microsoft's Azure Fiber effort. The only adjacent recent piece (2026-07-05 T-glass for AI servers) covers a different subject (chip substrate material), so there is no duplication.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: High-quality Analysis submission.
